state:
`Core\Request::jsonAs` has all its proofs: `about.md`, three examples, an attack
(`tests/hostile/core/Request/jsonAs/`), a bench, two Rust tests carrying `covers:` and the
existing conformance case. Its card in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/request.rs` is in the plain voice.

The attack found a crash, which is fixed: a document that hydrates a class containing itself
recursed natively with no stack check, so a deep enough chain ran past the stack floor. The
walk in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/json.rs`'s `decode_fields` now throws a catchable
`RecursionError` at the soft limit (`rule:errors/on-limit`), pinned by
`tests/conformance/core/a-json-chain-hydrated-near-the-stack-floor-throws-a-recursion-error.nvst`.

next.note: One slice is one feature with all its feature proofs, in file order:

backlog: Plain `Core\Json::decode` overflows the debug build's task stack between 600 and 800 nested levels; release decodes 1000. Whether the decoder should compare the stack as `decode_fields` now does is `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/json.rs`'s question.

`Core\Http\Response::jsonAs` and `Core\Arr::shapeAs` reach the same walk and can now throw `RecursionError`, and their cards do not list it (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/http.rs`, `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/arr.rs`).
